title: Privacy Policy
intro: The individual operator of MediFinder (the "Operator") establishes and discloses this Privacy Policy in accordance with the Personal Information Protection Act of Korea, in order to protect users' personal information and to handle related enquiries.

The Service has no sign-up process. It does not ask for identifying information such as name, date of birth, or contact details, and does not collect sensitive information such as treatment history or health status. The items listed below are generated automatically in the course of operating the Service, or are processed only when a user actively invokes a feature.
This is a translation of the Korean original. If the two versions differ, the Korean version prevails.

sections.heading: Article 1 (Categories of Personal Information and How It Is Collected)
blocks: (1) The Service processes the following information:

head: Category
Items
How it is collected
rows: IP address, time of access, requested URL, browser and operating system type (User-Agent), response status
Recorded automatically by the server and the content delivery network (CDN) when the Service is accessed.
Error message and location, URL at the time of the error, browser and operating system type, IP address
Sent automatically through an error tracking tool, and only when an error occurs.
Latitude and longitude of the device
Obtained from the device only when the user actively invokes a location feature. See Article 8.
Email address, contents of the enquiry
Only where a user contacts the Operator by email.

blocks: (2) The Service does not collect membership information such as name, date of birth, or contact details; sensitive information such as treatment history or health status; or unique identifiers such as resident registration numbers.
(3) The Service does not collect behavioural information and does not serve targeted advertising.

list: 1. Access logs: operating the Service, responding to incidents, and blocking abnormal bulk requests (security)
2. Error diagnostics: identifying the cause of errors and improving service quality
3. Location data: searching for nearby medical institutions and sorting by distance
4. Enquiry information: replying to enquiries and keeping a record of how they were handled

sections.heading: Article 3 (Retention Periods)

head: Category
Retention period
rows: Deleted automatically after up to 90 days, per the retention policy of the error tracking tool
Not stored on the server. Discarded immediately after search results are computed; on the device it may be reused briefly and is then discarded. Nothing remains once the browser or app is closed.
1 year after the enquiry is resolved

blocks: Where retention is required by law, the information is kept for the period required and then destroyed.

sections.heading: Article 4 (Provision to Third Parties)
blocks: The Operator does not provide personal information to third parties, except where required by law or where an investigative authority makes a request following the procedures prescribed by law.

sections.heading: Article 5 (Outsourcing of Processing)
blocks: (1) The Operator outsources processing as follows in order to provide the Service:

head: Processor
Outsourced work
rows: Delivery of web pages and traffic protection

blocks: (2) The outsourcing period matches the term of use of each service. Changes to the outsourced work or the processors will be disclosed by updating this policy.

sections.heading: Article 6 (Information Passed to Embedded Third-Party Services)
blocks: (1) The Service loads resources from the providers below in order to display maps and web fonts. In doing so the user's browser connects directly to those providers, so the IP address and request details reach them without passing through the Operator.

list: 1. NAVER Cloud Corp. — Naver Map display
2. Kakao Corp. — Kakao Map display
3. Google LLC — Google Maps display
4. jsDelivr — delivery of web fonts

blocks: (2) That processing is governed by each provider's own privacy policy.
(3) Maps are loaded only when the user opens the map screen or the corresponding map tab.

blocks: (1) Personal information is transferred abroad as follows:

head: Recipient

blocks: (2) Users may refuse the transfer of personal information abroad. However, these transfers are necessary to deliver and display the Service, so refusal means discontinuing use of the Service.

sections.heading: Article 8 (Processing of Personal Location Data)
blocks: (1) The Operator processes location data in accordance with the Act on the Protection and Use of Location Information of Korea.
(2) Location data is obtained from the device only when the user actively invokes a location feature. The Service does not track location in the background and does not record movement histories.
(3) Coordinates obtained are rounded to a grid of roughly 1 km before being sent with the search request. Precise coordinates never leave the device.
(4) Transmitted coordinates are used only to compute search results and are not stored on the server. They are not placed in the address bar or in shared links.
(5) The Operator does not provide personal location data to third parties.
(6) Users may refuse the collection of location data by any of the following means. The Service remains usable by selecting a region manually.

list: 1. Turning off location use within the Service
2. Blocking the location permission in the site settings of the browser
3. In the app, revoking the location permission under the operating system settings for app permissions

blocks: (7) Searches are processed by the HansApp API (api.plzhans.com), which the Operator also runs. The domain differs, but it is the same Operator’s server and does not constitute provision to a third party.

sections.heading: Article 9 (Destruction of Personal Information)
blocks: (1) Personal information is destroyed without delay once the retention period expires or the purpose of processing is achieved.
(2) Information stored in electronic files is deleted by technical means that make it unrecoverable. The Service does not keep printed copies of personal information.

sections.heading: Article 10 (Rights of Data Subjects and How to Exercise Them)
blocks: (1) Users may at any time request access to, correction of, deletion of, or suspension of the processing of their personal information.
(2) Such requests may be made by email to the contact in Article 14, and will be acted on without delay.

(3) Because the Service holds no information identifying users, a request for access or deletion must include details that allow the records to be identified (for example the time of access and the IP address). Requests that cannot be matched to specific records may not be actionable.
(4) Rights may also be exercised through a legal representative or an authorised agent.

sections.heading: Article 11 (Automatic Collection Devices and How to Refuse Them)
blocks: (1) The Service does not use cookies for tracking or advertising, and uses no analytics tools for traffic statistics or user profiling.
(2) The Service stores the following value in the browser's Local Storage. It stays on the device and is not sent to the server.

list: medifinder.geo.optOut — whether the user has turned off location use

blocks: (3) Users may delete this value at any time by clearing site data in their browser settings. Doing so does not restrict use of the Service.

sections.heading: Article 12 (Security Measures)
blocks: The Operator takes the following measures to keep personal information secure:

list: 1. Limiting the personal information processed to the minimum required to provide the Service
2. Encrypting communications between the Service and its servers (HTTPS)
3. Restricting and controlling access to servers and administrative tools
4. Rate limiting abnormal bulk requests

sections.heading: Article 13 (Children Under 14)
blocks: The Service has no sign-up process and does not collect personal information from children under the age of 14.

sections.heading: Article 14 (Privacy Officer)
blocks: (1) The Operator designates the following privacy officer, responsible for personal information processing and for handling enquiries and complaints from users:

list: Privacy officer: the Operator of the Service
Contact: medifinder.help@gmail.com

blocks: (2) Enquiries, complaints, and remedy requests concerning personal information may be sent to the contact above and will be answered without delay.

sections.heading: Article 15 (Remedies for Infringement of Rights)
blocks: Users may contact the following bodies for advice or dispute resolution regarding infringement of personal information:

list: Personal Information Infringement Report Centre (KISA): 118 / privacy.kisa.or.kr
Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee: +82-1833-6972 / www.kopico.go.kr
Supreme Prosecutors’ Office, Cyber Investigation Division: 1301 / www.spo.go.kr
National Police Agency, Cyber Bureau: 182 / ecrm.cyber.go.kr

sections.heading: Article 16 (Changes to This Policy)
blocks: Additions, deletions, or amendments to this policy are announced within the Service at least 7 days before they take effect, or at least 30 days in advance where the change materially affects the rights of users.

sections.heading: Addendum
blocks: This Privacy Policy takes effect on August 5, 2026.
